pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql: NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with a CHECK on the three values. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks the seeded rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected. The migrations are re-applied before every test (test/apply-migrations.js).
The 'AC-2' test asserts '— high' and '— low' after the title and nothing for normal. src/index.js `item` renders the label.
The 'AC-3' test covers high, low and normal, in id order, with ids inserted out of order (3, 1).
The 'AC-4' test checks that / lists all items in id order.
The 'AC-5' test checks the exact nav HTML for all four views; the current filter is a <strong>, not a link.
The 'AC-6' test checks High, urgent, empty and __proto__ each answer 400 with no <li>. src/index.js validates against a Set when the parameter is present.
The 'AC-7' test covers the no-match message for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' for an empty table in all four views.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. The 'AC-8' test asserts it. scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs now accepts a query string, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

findings.what: The fake app now records pathname plus search, but no test in the diff sends a route with a query through the traffic Worker and checks that the query reaches the app. The change is unexercised.
findings.fix: Add a traffic test that runs the Worker with '/?priority=high' in ROUTES and asserts that fakeApp.seen includes that exact path.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent and decisions: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled. Nothing is added beyond the ask except the traffic-config check relaxation, which the PR discloses and AC-8 needs.
All 8 acceptance items and all 4 state-table rows have a test that names them. No commit edits the spec after the go; the spec was added in the first commit.

`npm test` could not run here because vitest is not installed. I judged the tests by reading them. They assert behaviour, and the DB is reset and re-migrated before each test. No tests were deleted or loosened.
README describes the new filter. No stale references.
The priority value is validated against a Set and the query is parameterised. The empty-table versus no-match logic is correct.
The priority is bound as a parameter, never interpolated into SQL. The title is still HTML-escaped. The priority is only echoed after validation against the Set. No planted instructions found.
The page has only minimal server-rendered HTML and no stylesheets, components or client code to review.
No browser or UI flow is available in this session; the rendered HTML is covered by tests.
The PR's claims match the diff. The title is under 72 characters.
